doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Joining Maynard Ferguson's band and touring jazz clubs instead of moving to New York
summary: Recommended onto Maynard's band in 1999, Watkins became musical director within a year, touring clubs in New York, London and the US.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: an amazing drummer. So I’m getting just all this experience there. And then Maynard Ferguson would always have young guys in the band. And where they were from, it kind of moved like a wave. So if you had a lot of guys — if there were guys in the band from North Texas then they would recommend their buddies from North Texas. So there were some guys that got on to the band from Pittsburgh. And that began a wave, and then I got recommended onto the band and I subsequently recommended other people onto the band. So finally I was involved in jazz. So going with Maynard in 1999, by a year later I was musical director. And it was really worthwhile to me. I could write, I could play, I could meet other musicians, do record dates, go to New York. My experience in New York when I was with Maynard I would go to New York and live there for a week and play the Blue Note you know? Or go into the studio. And that happened a lot. It was the same thing with London. We would go and play Ronnie Scott’s for a week or two weeks, and these different places. And Seattle, Jazz Alley, Blues Alley, you know, all the different jazz clubs we’d go there for a week and we’d do it year after year. So that prevented me from moving to New York.
Because you had the income, you had the gig and you had the travel.
